stem: Which of the following causes jet black appearance of the pupillary aperture?

stem: Which of the following causes jet black appearance of the pupillary aperture?

stem: A 62-year-old diabetic woman with pre-existing proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) is at risk of developing which of the following?

stem: Which of the following is a cause of dilated fixed pupil?

explanation_verbatim: Causes of dilated fixed pupil → Trauma to the iris sphincter or the orbital parasympathetic nerves (traumatic mydriasis), Pharmacologic dilatation, Ciliary ganglion disease / damage, Oculomotor (III) Paralysis, Brain stem affection (dorsal midbrain syndrome), Stage III anaesthesia & Death (bilateral).

stem: Which of the following is considered a visual field defect that is characteristic of glaucoma?

printed_q: 20. Which of the following is considered a visual field defect that is characteristic of glaucoma?
stem: Which of the following is considered a visual field defect that is characteristic of glaucoma?

explanation_verbatim:
Characteristic field changes in glaucoma (particularly primary open angle glaucoma):
A. Paracentral scotomas: multiple isolated scotomata in the zone between 10 and 20 degrees from the fixation point.
B. Arcuate scotoma that arches above and below the fixation point.
C. Nasal step: Due to asymmetric involvement of the arcuate nerve bundles above and below the fixation point.
D. Tubular field (Tunnel vision): The field of vision may constrict until it is limited to a few degrees around fixation.
Fixation (central vision) may be spared until the disease is markedly advanced.
E. End-stage glaucoma: These residual seeing areas may be eventually lost leaving the patient blind.

stem: A 26-year-old male patient heads to the emergency department after getting injured in a quarrel. He reports that he got a fist blow trauma. Which of the following is the most common area fractured in that kind of trauma?

stem: Damage to which of the following structures causes corneal superficial vascularization and conjunctivalization of corneal epithelium?

explanation_verbatim: The conjunctiva at the limbus hosts the palisades of Vogt which contain the stem cells that provide regenerative cells to the corneal epithelium. stem: What is the grade of chemical eye injury that is characterized by total loss of corneal epithelium and stromal haze obscuring iris details?
What is the grade of chemical eye injury that is characterized by total loss of corneal epithelium and stromal haze obscuring iris details?
explanation_verbatim:
Grading of chemical eye injuries →
A. Grade 1: (excellent prognosis): Clear cornea (epithelial damage only) and no limbal ischaemia.
B. Grade 2: (good prognosis): Hazy cornea but with visible iris detail and less than 30% limbal ischaemia.

stem: A 6-month-old child presented with epiphora due to nasolacrimal duct obstruction. Pressure over lacrimal sac caused reflux of mucus from lacrimal punctum. What's the best management for that child?
options: Lacrimal sac massage and probing surgery if no response after 1 year of age

Treatment of nasolacrimal system abnormalities (congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction):
A. About 85% of cases resolve without surgical intervention before the first year. Therefore, surgery is not indicated before the first year of life. Massage over the lacrimal sac at the medial corner of the eyelid to increase pressure in the canal.

stem: Which of the following is characteristic of comitant strabismus?
options: Degree of misalignment varies with gaze
Degree of misalignment is equal in all directions of gaze
Caused by orbital disease or trauma
explanation_verbatim:
Types of strabismus according to comitance:
A. Comitant strabismus: the angle (or degree) of misalignment is approximately equal in all directions of gaze. Concomitant strabismus in patients under age 6 is rarely caused by serious neurologic disease. Strabismus arising later in life may have a specific and serious neurologic basis.
B. Incomitant strabismus: the degree of misalignment varies with the direction of gaze. This type may indicate neurologic disorder, such as third nerve palsy, or orbital disease or trauma, such as thyroid ophthalmopathy or blowout fracture.

Acute unilateral diminution of vision.
